learning_outcomes.text: Will understand and be able to apply the basic concepts of calculus in one and several variables.
Will understand and be able to apply the basic concepts of numerical calculus.
Will understand the terminology, notation, and methods of Mathematics.
Will know specific software for solving mathematical problems.
Will be able to use abstraction mechanisms as a tool to help solve real-world problems.

syllabus_topics: Numbers and functions. - Real numbers: operations, properties and order relation. - Intervals. Absolute value and distance. - Rational exponent powers and radicals. - Functions of a real variable: previous definitions, classification and operations; elementary functions: polynomial, logarithm, exponential, trigonometric and hyperbolic.

Continuity and differentiation. - Limit at a point: lateral limits and existence. Limit at extremes. Operations with limits. Indeterminations. Equivalences. - Continuity at a point. Discontinuities. - Continuity in an interval. Bolzano's theorem and its consequences. - Differentiation at a point. Derivative function. Calculation of derivatives. - Lagrange's mean value theorem and its consequences. - Applications: study of functions. - L'Hopital's rule. Comparison of infinities.

Integration - Definition of integral. Geometric interpretation. Integrability and properties. - Definition of antiderivative. Barrow's rule. Fundamental theorem of calculus. - Calculation of integrals and antiderivatives: change of variable and integration by parts. Antiderivatives of rational, trigonometric and irrational functions. - Improper integrals: Euler's Gamma and Beta functions. - Applications of the integral: length, area and volume.

Complex numbers - Definition. The complex plane: modulus and principal argument. - Representations and operations. - Polynomials with complex coefficients. The fundamental theorem of algebra. - Roots of complex numbers.
Fourier Series - Numerical series. - Power series: Taylor and Laurent series. - Scalar product and oscillation. Trigonometric series. Fourier series: phase and harmonics.
Numerical methods - Absolute and relative errors. - Numerical solution of equations: Newton's method and secant method. - Numerical integration: Newton-Cotes formulas.
Computer Practices - Introduction to Sage. Differential and integral calculus. Programming of numerical methods.
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 25% from a non-recoverable partial written test, 60% from written exams (recoverable), and 15% from practice reports. To pass, a minimum of 40% must be achieved in the written exams component and at least 25% in the practice reports component. If these minimums are not met, the final grade will be 'Fail', capped at 4.5.
